371165.title: Hamiltonicity conjecture for connected bicirculants
371165.literal_statement:
A **bicirculant** is a regular graph admitting a semiregular automorphism with two vertex-orbits of equal size. Let $G(m,2)$ denote the generalized Petersen graph with parameter $m$, and let $K_2$ be the complete graph on two vertices.

**Hamiltonicity conjecture.** Every connected bicirculant, except for the complete graph $K_2$ and the generalized Petersen graphs $G(m,2)$ with

$$
m\equiv 5\pmod 6,
$$

is hamiltonian.

This conjecture seeks a complete classification of non-hamiltonian bicirculants. It extends Alspach's classification for generalized Petersen graphs and the corresponding result for $I$-graphs; the conjecture remains open in the source.
371165.finding: Hamilton cycle splicing would need a compatible spanning cycle in every spoke component, including cyclic Haar graphs with composite orbit size. The 2026 journal result retrieved in search proves restricted spoke/arithmetic cases, not the full claim.
371165.precise_gap_or_exclusion: General cyclic Haar cases and compatibility of the component splices remain unproved; journal proof bodies not fully reviewed.
371165.review_depth: literal statement and live arXiv version metadata only (except noted web journal routing)

371166.title: Triply-transitivity conjecture for collinearity graphs of elliptic polar spaces
371166.literal_statement: Let $q$ be a prime power, and let the collinearity graph of the polar space $\mathcal{Q}^{-}(5,q)$ be the graph whose vertices are the points of $\mathcal{Q}^{-}(5,q)$, with two vertices adjacent when they are collinear. **Triply-transitivity conjecture.** For any prime power $q$, the collinearity graph of the polar space $\mathcal{Q}^{-}(5,q)$ is triply-transitive. This is one of the two infinite families left unresolved in the near-complete classification of triply-transitive strongly regular graphs; it is supported by analysis of small examples, but its general validity remains open.
371166.finding: Ordinary permutation-group triple transitivity would fail for any noncomplete graph, but that is not a legitimate refutation of the source-specific triply-transitive graph property.
371166.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Read the actual graph property, polar-space form and orbit theorem before attempting an in-scope triple witness; primary body unread.

371261.title: Vanishing conjecture for the cubic generators of dual matroid toric ideals
371261.literal_statement:
Let $L$ be a linear subspace of dimension $r$ whose matroid $\mathrm{M}(L)$ is connected. Set $\mathcal E_L=\mathcal S_L\oplus\mathcal Q_L$. **Vanishing conjecture for dual matroid cubics.** The vector bundle

$$
\bigwedge^{r}\mathcal E_L^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^{r}\mathcal E_L^\vee\otimes\det\mathcal Q_L
$$

has vanishing $H^1$. The prediction is motivated by the absence of cubic minimal generators for the toric ideal of the dual matroid, but the source does not specify its resolution status.
371261.finding: Quadratic generation of a matroid toric ideal alone does not identify this H1 group; the displayed bundle has repeated exterior-power factors and requires the wonderful-variety cohomological bridge.
371261.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need actual base variety, bundle definitions and complete vanishing theorem or explicit nonzero cohomology; body unread.

371399.title: Conjectural basis for box-product spaces of qMZV words
371399.literal_statement:
For $1\leq z\leq d$, let $\mathfrak{M}_{z,d}$ be the recursively defined set of plain basis vectors, and define

$$
\mathfrak{B}_{z,d}:=\left\{u_{n_1}\cdots u_{n_s}\boxast u_{\ell_1}\cdots u_{\ell_d}:\begin{array}{l}u_{\ell_1}\cdots u_{\ell_d}\in\mathfrak{M}_{z,d},\ n_j\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0},\\ n_1+\cdots+n_s+\ell_1+\cdots+\ell_d=z+d,\\ \ell_1>z-d+\delta_{n_1=s=1}\end{array}\right\}.
$$

**Basis conjecture.** For $1\leq z\leq d$, $\mathfrak{B}_{z,d}$ is a basis of $\mathscr{S}_{z,d}$. The set was obtained from numerical calculations, and the paper postpones a proof to future work.
371399.finding: A triangular leading-word argument must give distinct pivots for all z,d and show every word reduces to those pivots. Prior allowlisted work on 371398 only treated the related box-kernel question and source small cases.
371399.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Recursive M definition, product identities and uniform spanning/independence proof unpaid; no rank search performed.

371401.title: Edge-count conjecture for minimal kinematics graphs
371401.literal_statement: Let $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, and call a graph on $[n]$ a **minimal kinematics graph** when its edge set is inclusion-maximal among the graphs realizing minimal kinematics. **Minimal kinematics edge-count conjecture.** Every minimal kinematics graph on $[n]$ has $3n-6$ edges. The conjecture is consistent with the authors' data and with the results cited as EPS; it extends the observed $2$-tree examples, but remains unproved in the supplied text.

371476.title: Existence conjecture for Butson Hadamard matrices of order $2p+4$
371476.literal_statement: A Butson Hadamard matrix $BH(n,q)$ is an $n\times n$ complex matrix whose entries are $q$th roots of unity and whose rows are pairwise orthogonal under the standard complex inner product. **Existence conjecture.** For any prime $p$, Butson Hadamard matrices $BH(2p+4,2p)$ exist. The conjecture concerns the existence of a family of Butson Hadamard matrices at the parameters $(n,q)=(2p+4,2p)$; characterizing all pairs $(n,q)$ for which such matrices exist remains a fundamental open problem.
371476.finding: A single Fourier/Kronecker construction does not yield size 2p+4 for every prime p; root-of-unity order and orthogonality both matter.
371476.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need a uniform all-prime block construction or genuine arithmetic nonexistence obstruction at an assigned parameter. No matrix search.

371535.title: The TN-poset to UMEL-shellability conjecture for geometric lattices
371535.literal_statement: Let $\mathrm{M}$ be a matroid. A **TN-poset** is a lower rank-uniform poset whose lower triangular matrix of lower Whitney numbers of the second kind is totally nonnegative, and **UMEL-shellable** refers to the shellability property defined in the source. **The TN-poset to UMEL-shellability conjecture.** If $\mathcal{L}(\mathrm{M})$ is a TN-poset, then $\mathcal{L}(\mathrm{M})$ is UMEL-shellable. The converse is false, as partition lattices are UMEL-shellable but not TN-posets; the forward implication is supported by rank-uniformity results, but the source gives no proof or resolution.
371535.finding: Total nonnegativity constrains Whitney numbers but supplies no chain labels or unique rising chains by itself. The partition-lattice converse counterexample is the wrong implication.

371659.title: Average-rarity conjecture for rooted-set representations
371659.literal_statement:
Let $V$ be a finite ground set, and let $\mathcal C$ be an intersection-closed family on $V$ containing $\varnothing$. Suppose that $\mathcal C$ admits a rooted-set representation in which every element of $V$ is the root of at most one rooted set. **Average-rarity conjecture.** Then $\mathcal C$ is average-rare.

The paper proves average-rarity for order-ideal families of functional preorders, a special case in which the rooted-set stems are singletons. The conjecture extends this result to rooted sets with larger stems; existence of a rare element is known in the relevant general setting, but the stronger average-rarity assertion remains open.
371659.finding: Exact Horn-system NDS decomposition and two induction failures are given in ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md. Functional-preorder proof read, including its forest decomposition.
371659.precise_gap_or_exclusion: No sign bound for the conditioned families and no induction preserving the one-rule-per-root hypothesis; full Conjecture 6.1 unresolved here.
371659.review_depth: literal and live arXiv version metadata; selected definitions and theorem/proof passages

371698.title: Strict realizability conjecture for $K_{2,3}^{'}$-free graphs
371698.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $Y_G$ denote its strict realization space, and let $\mathcal{R}_\ell$ denote the relevant matroid or independence structure. A graph is $K_{2,3}^{'}$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $K_{2,3}^{'}$.

**Strict realizability conjecture.** If $G$ is a $K_{2,3}^{'}$-free graph which is independent in $\mathcal{R}_\ell$, then

$$
Y_G \neq \emptyset.
$$

This gives a sufficient condition for strict realizability. The source presents it as a conjecture following examples of graphs that are not strictly realizable.
371698.finding: Generic realizability of a matroid-independent incidence pattern need not avoid every undesired line incidence. It is the strict open locus Y_G that must be nonempty.
371698.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Actual realization scheme and R_l independence criterion unread; no exact graph plus emptiness proof.

371720.title: Hibi–Qureshi toric characterization of simple polyominoes
371720.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a polyomino, and let $I_{\mathcal{P}}$ denote its polyomino ideal. A polyomino $\mathcal{P}$ is **simple** when it has no holes. The toric ideal of the edge ring of a finite simple graph is the kernel of the monomial map defining that edge ring.

**Hibi–Qureshi conjecture.** The ideal $I_{\mathcal{P}}$ arises as the toric ideal of the edge ring of a finite simple graph if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ is simple.

Simple polyominoes are known to admit such a toric description through an associated bipartite graph. The conjecture asserts that this phenomenon characterizes simplicity and therefore cannot generally extend to non-simple polyominoes.
371720.finding: Survey Conjecture 3.1 is exact. Theorem 3.2 excludes complement polyominoes of a simple internal region, not every nonsimple polyomino. Prime or toric by some monomial map is not equivalent to being a graph edge toric ideal.
371720.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need the arbitrary-hole graph-kernel obstruction or a nonsimple polyomino with an exact edge-ring presentation; journal body and cited predecessor proofs unread.
371720.review_depth: literal and live arXiv version metadata; selected definitions and theorem/proof passages

371726.title: Nill's facet-number conjecture for reflexive polytopes
371726.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathcal P}$ be a $d$-dimensional reflexive polytope, and let $N({\mathcal P})$ denote its number of facets.

**Nill's conjecture.**

$$
N({\mathcal P}) \le 6^{d/2}.
$$

This conjecture concerns a uniform upper bound on the number of facets of reflexive polytopes in terms of their dimension. The paper proves the bound for twinned chain polytopes, giving a partial answer; the general conjecture remains open.
371726.finding: Products of reflexive hexagons meet the even-dimensional scale but establish lower examples, not an upper bound for every reflexive polytope.
371726.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need full-dimensional universal facet argument or an explicit reflexive violating polytope; v2 body unread.

371734.title: The move-connectivity conjecture for rotationally symmetric plabic graphs
371734.literal_statement:
Let $G$ and $G'$ be minimal rotationally symmetric plabic graphs, and let $f_G$ and $f_{G'}$ denote their associated permutations.

**Move-connectivity conjecture.** If

$$
f_G=f_{G'},
$$

then $G$ and $G'$ are related through a sequence of rotationally symmetric moves.

Each rotationally symmetric move preserves the associated permutation, so the conjecture asks whether all minimal rotationally symmetric representatives of a given permutation lie in one move-equivalence class. This is presented as an expected extension of the preceding lemma and is not proved in the supplied text.
371734.finding: Ordinary plabic move connectivity does not give symmetric move connectivity: applying a move to each rotation can fail when translates overlap.
371734.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need equivariant reduction with compatible overlapping moves or exact inequivalent symmetric representatives; primary move definitions unread.

371828.title: The homotopy conjecture for total 2-cut complexes of cycle powers in the intermediate range
371828.literal_statement:
Let $C_n^p$ be the $p$th power of the cycle graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\Delta_{2}^t(C_n^p)$ denote its total $2$-cut complex. Let $2p+3\leq n\leq3p$, and let $r$ be a positive integer satisfying

$$
2p+\frac{p}{r+1}<n\leq2p+\frac{p}{r}.
$$

**The intermediate-range homotopy conjecture.** If $n=2p+\frac{p}{r}$, then

$$
\Delta_{2}^t(C_n^p)\simeq\bigvee_{n-2p-1}\mathbb{S}^{n-2r-3}.
$$

If $2p+\frac{p}{r+1}<n<2p+\frac{p}{r}$, then

$$
\Delta_{2}^t(C_n^p)\simeq\mathbb{S}^{n-2r-4}.
$$

record.statement:

\Delta_{2}^t(C_n^p)\simeq\mathbb{S}^{n-2r-4}.
$$

371854.title: Reduced form conjecture for shortest separating non-contractible cycles
371854.literal_statement:
A **separating non-contractible cycle** (SNCC) is a cycle in a triangulation that is separating and non-contractible. Let $t$ be a triangulation and let $C$ be an SNCC of $t$ of shortest length. **Shortest SNCC reduction conjecture.** It is impossible to write

$$
C=\gamma^2C',
$$

where $\gamma$ is a simple cycle.

This is a deterministic conjecture about the structure of a shortest separating non-contractible cycle. The paper presents it as a further open question at the end of its discussion of conjectures.
371854.finding: A simple graph-theoretic cycle cannot traverse gamma twice, but SNCC here must be interpreted in the source topological/walk convention. Declaring the word reduced by definition is not a new proof.

371995.title: 6-color conjecture for cubic bipartite planar graph squares
371995.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic bipartite planar graph, and let $G^2$ be its square, obtained by joining vertices at distance at most $2$ in $G$. Let $\chi(G^2)$ denote the chromatic number of $G^2$.

**Cubic bipartite planar square-coloring conjecture.** The square satisfies

$$
\chi(G^2)\leq 6.
$$

This is a strengthening of the general cubic planar bound in Wegner's conjecture and is presented as an open problem for cubic bipartite planar graphs.
371995.finding: A 3-coloring of the distance-two constraints on each bipartition would combine to a 6-coloring of the square, but those half-squares need not each be 3-colorable by elementary planar coloring.
371995.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need compatible global 6-coloring or exact cubic bipartite planar counterexample with chi(square)>=7. No coloring search.

372043.title: The zero-forcing consequence of the minimal-forts bound
372043.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $n$ be its order, and let $\mathcal{F}_G$ denote the family of minimal forts of $G$. Let $\operatorname{Z}(G)$ denote the zero forcing number of $G$. **Zero-forcing consequence conjecture.** If

$$
\lvert\mathcal{F}_G\rvert = n/3,
$$

then

$$
\operatorname{Z}(G)=n/3.
$$

The paper presents this as an observation supported by examples and by a proposition relating minimal forts, fort number, and zero forcing number; no general proof or resolution is supplied.
372043.finding: Zero forcing is the transversal number of minimal forts. The desired equality is equivalent to pairwise disjointness of all minimal forts when their number is n/3. The full reduction and failure of the tree-to-graph extension are recorded.
372043.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Missing extremal rigidity: intersecting minimal forts imply more than n/3 minimal forts. Neither source tree theorem nor Proposition 5.4 proves that premise.

372051.title: Jensen–Len tropical Martens conjecture for metric graphs
372051.literal_statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a metric graph of genus $g$, and let $d,r$ be integers satisfying $0<2r\leq d<g$. The Brill–Noether rank $w_d^r(\Gamma)$ is the tropical Brill–Noether rank. **Jensen–Len tropical Martens conjecture.** One has

$$
w_d^r(\Gamma)\leq d-2r,
$$

and equality holds precisely when $\Gamma$ is hyperelliptic. This conjecture seeks a tropical analogue of Martens' theorem using Brill–Noether rank rather than the dimension of the Brill–Noether locus; the preceding proposition establishes the inequality and equality for hyperelliptic graphs, while the asserted converse is the conjectural part.
372051.finding: The hyperelliptic direction plus the inequality does not prove that equality forces hyperellipticity. A rank-1 degree-2 test is only a small subcase.
372051.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need exact tropical Brill-Noether rank definition and all d,r converse mechanism; source proof body unread.

372053.title: Fau's graph-algebra nowhere-scatteredness conjecture
372053.literal_statement:
Let $E$ be a row-finite graph, and let $C^*(E)$ denote its graph $C^*$-algebra. The algebra $C^*(E)$ is **nowhere scattered** when it has no nonzero scattered quotient. The graph $E$ is said to have Condition (K) and distinct detours as in the source.

**Fau's graph-algebra conjecture.** $C^*(E)$ is nowhere scattered if and only if $C^*(E)$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable, if and only if $E$ has Condition (K) and distinct detours.

This is a characterization of nowhere scatteredness for graph $C^*$-algebras in terms of regularity of the algebra and combinatorial properties of the graph. The supplied text gives a related theorem for finite graphs, but does not establish the stated row-finite formulation.
372053.finding: Passing finite graph Z-stability to an arbitrary row-finite graph requires appropriate algebraic approximation and preservation of the graph conditions. Finite induced subgraphs are not automatically the required algebraic building blocks.
372053.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Condition (K), distinct detours and the row-finite exhaustion bridge unread/unproved. No infinite operator-algebra endpoint.

372168.title: Forbidden connected subsequences in bounded confidence processes
372168.literal_statement: Let $(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be a sequence of cluster sizes of a bounded confidence (BC) process. A subsequence is **connected** when its corresponding clusters are connected in the final configuration. **Forbidden-subsequence conjecture.** There cannot be a connected subsequence $(1,1,1,1)$ or $(2,2,1,1,1,2,2)$. This would constrain the possible cluster-size patterns and may help establish upper bounds on the number of connected components. The claim is presented as a conjecture, and no resolution is given in the source.
372168.finding: Local splitting inequalities and ordered averaging yield a concrete charging route, but the necessary all-time disjoint-reservoir lemma is missing. Final clusters are mutually disconnected, so the corpus gloss of connected subsequence cannot be used literally.
372168.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Source Conjecture 1 wording read; connected-subsequence semantics and a time-uniform reservoir bound both remain necessary. No solver or trajectory enumeration.
